growth_signal.value: Named Victorian Start-Up of the Year, and its funding grew from an earlier $10M round to a $45M round used to expand into Europe.

raised.value: About $45M AUD (reported elsewhere as $29.6M) including a round for European expansion

entry.idea: Homes with solar panels and batteries usually get a flat, poor rate from their electricity company, so Amber sells power at the real wholesale price and its software buys and sells energy from a home battery automatically at the best times.
entry.lesson: Turn a flat, boring price (electricity) into something that trades automatically for the customer, and you can charge for the software that does the trading.
entry.name: Amber

growth.basis: substitute: funding round size (grew from about $10M to $45M)
growth.reason: No customer or revenue numbers were given, but the funding round grew sharply, from about $10M to $45M, and paid for a move into Europe, which is a strong signal from investors.

market.reason: Selling wholesale-priced power and automated battery trading is a real business for homeowners in Australia, and the move into Europe could grow it, but it is still a niche within the wider energy market.

tech.reason: Automatically trading a home battery against changing wholesale power prices is solid software engineering, but a well-funded competitor could build something similar within a year or two.

entry.twist: Its SmartShift software watches live wholesale electricity prices and moves a customer's battery for them, and the company has now taken this model from Australia into Europe.
entry.who_pays: Homeowners with solar panels and batteries who switch their electricity plan to Amber.
entry.why_now: More homes are installing solar panels and batteries, and new government rebates for home batteries make it worth switching to a retailer that can get more value out of them.
